recipe.title: Porridge with apple and rhubarb compote
recipe.intro: British apples from store are still crisp and sweet in March, and the first pink rhubarb gives them a sharp, bright lift for a warming breakfast.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until they start to pop and smell nutty. Tip onto a plate.
Put the apples, rhubarb, orange zest and juice, cinnamon, sugar and 3 tbsp water in a saucepan. Stir, cover and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the apples are tender and the rhubarb has collapsed into a soft pink sauce.
Meanwhile, put the oats, 1.2 litres water and a pinch of salt in another pan. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, top with the warm compote and scatter over the toasted seeds.
recipe.tip: Make a double batch of compote. It keeps for 4 days in the fridge and is just as good cold on toast.
